text:
Calculate the moles of acid and hydroxide:

- \(n(\mathrm{CH_3COOH})=(0.500)(0.1)=0.050\ \mathrm{mol}\)
- \(n(\mathrm{HCl})=(0.400)(0.2)=0.080\ \mathrm{mol}\)
- \(n(\mathrm{Ba(OH)_2})=(0.300)(0.3)=0.090\ \mathrm{mol}\)

Each mole of \(\mathrm{Ba(OH)_2}\) produces two moles of \(\mathrm{OH^-}\):

\[
n(\mathrm{OH^-})=2(0.090)=0.180\ \mathrm{mol}
\]

Total acidic equivalents:

\[
0.050+0.080=0.130\ \mathrm{mol}
\]

Excess hydroxide:

\[
0.180-0.130=0.050\ \mathrm{mol}
\]

Total volume:

\[
0.500+0.400+0.300=1.200\ \mathrm{L}
\]

\[
[\mathrm{OH^-}]=\frac{0.050}{1.200}=0.04167\ \mathrm{M}
\]

\[
\mathrm{pOH}=-\log(0.04167)=1.38
\]

\[
\mathrm{pH}=14.00-1.38=12.62
\]

Answer: C
